clue.text: Murderer's throttling prone officers

indicators.note: to throttle is to grip round the throat, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: Cain, the Bible's first murderer, with the possessive S
prone to something means apt to do it

explanation.surface: A killer strangles some army officers who are lying face down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone' looks physical (lying flat) but means inclined, APT. The possessive 's of 'Murderer's' supplies a real S here.
explanation.definitionFit: Captains are commissioned ranks in the army and navy, and leaders of ships, so they are officers.

clue.text: A form of super-poll, covering every question?

indicators.note: a new form of a word is its letters set out in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, its nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge opinion survey that asks about everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: something useful for every purpose would, in this poll's world, cover every question.
explanation.definitionFit: General-use, versatile things serve every need, which the question mark stretches to a survey dealing with every query.

clue.text: Lose interest after stomaching a Director's outburst

indicators.note: to stomach something is to take it inside one's belly, so the word goes round other letters

parts.note: to tire of something is to lose interest in it
D is a standard abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: Someone gets bored and then swallows a film director's angry rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomaching' looks like tolerating, but here it means holding in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, an outburst of denunciation.

clue.text: I continue blocking nice working, being unyielding

indicators.note: one word blocks another by sitting in the middle of it
working here means being worked on, the letters kneaded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, four letters to be rearranged
to last is to continue or go on

explanation.surface: Someone keeps obstructing a pleasant job, refusing to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' gives NEIC, and 'blocking' sets the verb for going on inside it; 'being' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic materials do not stretch or give, so they are rigid and unbending.

clue.text: Deity placed to get your following

parts.note: something placed somewhere has been sat there

explanation.surface: A god is set in position so that your followers gather round.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a woodland demigod of Greek myth, part man and part goat, so a minor deity.

clue.text: Notorious school — rebellious tsarina in it, leading bridge team

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lead, coming in front of the other piece
rebels refuse to stay in line, so these letters break ranks into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters to be rearranged
in bridge, North and South are partners, so NS is a team

explanation.surface: An infamous school where an unruly Russian empress attends and captains the bridge side.
explanation.walkthrough: St Trinian's is the anarchic fictional girls' school of Ronald Searle's cartoons and British comedy films.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional school is famous for its wild, lawless pupils, so it is notorious.

clue.text: Hat in brown shades kept up disorderly show

indicators.note: one word goes in the middle of another
in a down entry, kept up means held upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: tans are shades of brown
a kepi is a French military cap with a flat top

explanation.surface: A hat in brown colours is held aloft during a chaotic performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept up' turns TANS into SNAT, and the hat goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake pit is a scene of chaos and vicious struggle, a disorderly spectacle.

clue.text: Couple: one with one following half-heartedly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of the heart of a four-letter word is removed, one of its two central letters

parts.note: a team's following, its body of supporters, is loosely the team

explanation.surface: Two people pair up: one person and another trailing after without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' takes away one of the two middle letters EA, leaving TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair in a romantic relationship is called an item in everyday speech.

clue.text: Hunt coming up empty

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a meet is the gathering of a fox hunt before it sets off

explanation.surface: A hunt rides home having caught nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: TEEM in the sense of pouring out is a dialect and technical use, as in teeming molten metal from a ladle.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to pour out or drain a vessel, so it can mean to empty.

clue.text: California stories involving one measure of heat

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold or include, so one piece holds another

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional tales
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: West Coast tales that include a way of gauging temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A calorie is a unit of energy defined by the heat needed to warm water by one degree.

clue.text: Tintagel, say, its exterior beset by some action

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: a case is a legal action, a lawsuit
its refers back to Tintagel, whose outside letters are T and L

explanation.surface: The Cornish fortress is besieged around its walls by attackers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintagel is a ruined clifftop fortress in Cornwall linked with King Arthur. 'its' does double duty, pointing back to that word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish ruin is an example of a fortified stronghold, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: What involves physical exercise in tent's ultimate level?

definitions.text: What involves physical exercise in tent's ultimate level?

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the closing letter of the word is used
one piece goes in the middle of another

parts.note: to raze a building is to level it to the ground
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A riddle about some athletic activity at the top of a big tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a circus swing high in the big top, while also building the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar hung high for acrobats sits at the top level of a circus tent and demands athletic effort.

clue.text: Source of detonation possibly producing broader ruins

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An explosion's cause may be producing wider wreckage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'detonation' is the sonic boom a jet makes, not a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking the speed-of-sound threshold creates a sonic boom, an explosive noise.

clue.text: Comes up against information not including opening of gay bars

indicators.note: the named letter is left out of the word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: counters are the bars at which pubs serve drinks

explanation.surface: Someone runs into news that leaves out certain bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter something is to meet or confront it, often unexpectedly.

clue.text: Succeeded in avoiding hill run

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of a letter, so it is taken out

parts.note: a slope is a hillside
S is a genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A runner did well by steering clear of the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to move with long easy strides, a relaxed run.

clue.text: See 6
After reorganisation, Princeton's dropping new assessor

indicators.note: reorganising puts the letters in a new order
to drop a letter is to let it fall out

parts.note: the university's name with its S

explanation.surface: Once restructured, Princeton University abandons a novel examiner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes one of the two Ns; the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who examines and evaluates, so an assessor.

clue.text: Unaccompanied, getting stuck into unknown sticky stuff, picking up knowledge of wine

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up means lifting, reading from the bottom upwards
being stuck into something is being lodged inside it

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
someone unaccompanied is alone
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A lone person stuck in some mysterious glue starts learning about wine.
explanation.walkthrough: LONE goes inside YGOO to make YGOLONEO, which 'picking up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Oenology is the scientific study of wines and winemaking.

clue.text: French composer's musical academy on the water in Paris

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: RAM is the Royal Academy of Music in London
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A French composer's music school sits by a river in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Philippe Rameau was a leading French Baroque composer of operas and keyboard music.

clue.text: Core matters enclosed in letters

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of another

parts.note: esses are the letter S, plural
enc. is a standard abbreviation for enclosed, written on letters

explanation.surface: Key matters are tucked inside some correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like mail, which fits the enclosure, but it means the letter S written out, ESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is the fundamental nature of something, so essences are core matters.

clue.text: A vet returned in closing feature

indicators.note: returned means sent back, the letters read in reverse order

parts.note: a vet, an animal doctor, is a doc

explanation.surface: A vet came back for a final appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, its closing feature.

clue.text: British poet's line receiving Arab agreement? On the contrary

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay

parts.note: Ar. is a standard abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, one piece holding another
the clue says the line receives, but it is the other way round: the line is taken in

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

explanation.surface: A poet's verse line wins an Arab's approval, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian poet, author of Dover Beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold is a well-known nineteenth-century English poet and critic.

clue.text: Frantically raced with fortune available here?

definitions.text: Frantically raced with fortune available here?

indicators.note: frantic means wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Riders sped wildly, with a fortune to be won here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the event: cyclists race hard with prize money and glory at stake.
explanation.definitionFit: The great French cycling stage race is where riders race frantically for big rewards.

clue.text: Make a new plan, with money that's coming in cut

indicators.note: one letter comes into the middle of another word

parts.note: to reap a crop is to cut it
M is a standard abbreviation for money in economics

explanation.surface: Someone redesigns a scheme once incoming cash is reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To remap is to draw a fresh map, hence to lay out a plan again.

clue.text: It's very good in choking millions?

definitions.text: It's very good in choking millions?

indicators.note: to choke is to grip the throat, so the outer letters close round one

parts.note: so means very, as in so happy

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark: something is excellent at suffocating huge numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes urban pollution, which is very good at choking millions of city dwellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted fog hangs over cities and makes breathing hard for their millions of inhabitants.

clue.text: What'll make you black and blue?

definitions.text: What'll make you black and blue?

parts.words: What'll make you black and blue?
parts.note: black and blue means bruised, so the clue asks what causes bruises

explanation.surface: A question about what turns you dark colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Black and blue sounds like colours or a sports kit, but it is the bruised look after a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard knock or punch leaves bruises, the purplish marks of injury.

clue.text: Company investing in shops beginning to match leader in Scotland

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or put in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a mall is a set of shops

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A firm puts money into retail outlets to rival a top Scottish figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing in' looks financial but means placing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm was the name of several medieval kings of Scots, notably the one who defeated Macbeth.

clue.text: US writer's article securing gold and more gold

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, the word gripping another inside it

parts.note: the is the definite article
or is the heraldic term for gold
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An American author's piece locks away gold and then extra gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing, which fits the author, but it is grammar's THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was a nineteenth-century American author, famous for Walden.

clue.text: Happy to embrace week of unco-ordinated style

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, wrapping round another piece

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy and carefree

explanation.surface: A cheerful person hugs a week of clumsy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawky describes an awkward, ungainly manner, lacking physical co-ordination.

clue.text: Promotional item is restricted by cut in description of holiday destination?

indicators.note: restricted means hemmed in, so the inner piece is held inside

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
an ad is an advertisement, promoting a product

explanation.surface: A cut-price advert describes a dream holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'paradise' is how brochures describe resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel brochures habitually call idyllic resorts heaven on earth, a perfect place.
